claims.harm: a monolithic commit combining unrelated changes makes meaningful review difficult
claims.quote: There's a single commit here with a lot of changes that don't look closely related... though in this current state I can't do that meaningfully.

claims.author: l0rinc
claims.harm: setting -loglevel unintentionally enables a log category without -debug being set
claims.quote: Previously, setting a category level at startup stored the override, but it had no visible effect unless the category was also enabled with -debug. Here, setting `-loglevel=net:trace` appears to enable net by itself.

status_by.quote: It's fixed by making `-loglevel` only update the levels of previously enabled categories.

claims.author: l0rinc
claims.harm: confusing design that forces conditional categories and unconditional logging levels into the same model
claims.quote: Seems we have two fundamentally different ways of logging that we're forcing together here... I find this design confusing for multiple reasons

status_by.quote: changed array declaration and added comment to make this clearer

claims.author: l0rinc
claims.harm: lack of test coverage for the runtime-enable behavior where categories default to Debug even if configured at Trace at startup
claims.quote: Could we add a test that goes through this runtime-enable path after startup configured the category at Trace?

status_by.quote: adding new tests commits before changes to cover more behaviors

claims.author: l0rinc
claims.harm: kernel logging API changes behavior by enabling a category when setting its level
claims.quote: Previously, setting a category level did not enable the category. Now it looks like setting the level also enables it. Should we adjust this to match the old behavior?

status_by.quote: In this case I think the new behavior is probably better as there is no point to kernel code setting a level for a category that is ignored because the category is enabled.
